claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and ascetic who lived approximately c. 185 – c. 253.
The Philocalia is an anthology of Origen's texts, probably compiled by Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen.
Basil the Great was bishop of Caesarea and lived approximately 329–379.

The Philocalia was probably compiled during Basil and Gregory's monastic retreat in Pontus in the late 350s to early 360s, or in any event early in their careers and before their own theological writings.
Opinion is divided about who compiled the Philocalia, with some scholars questioning the traditional attribution to Basil and Gregory.
Many of Origen's works are lost, and consequently the extracts in the anthology are valuable today.
The Philocalia comprises twenty-seven chapters, each providing an excerpt or multiple extracts from Origen's works.
About a fifth of the Philocalia is taken from Contra Celsum.

The extracts include long selections from Origen's speculative theological treatise 'On First Principles' and his apologetic 'Against Celsus', as well as extracts from his biblical homilies and commentaries and an excerpt from one of his letters.
